questions.q: State the law of demand and explain the law of diminishing marginal utility that underlies it.

answer.text: The law of demand states that, other things remaining equal, the quantity of a good that a consumer buys rises when its price falls, and falls when its price rises. There is thus an inverse relationship between the price of a good and the quantity demanded, which is why the demand curve slopes downward from left to right.

This behaviour is explained by the law of diminishing marginal utility. Marginal utility is the extra satisfaction a consumer gets from consuming one more unit of a good. As a person consumes more and more of a good, the satisfaction from each additional unit becomes smaller. So a consumer is willing to buy extra units only if the price falls to match the lower satisfaction they give.
A consumer buys a good up to the point where its marginal utility equals its price.

answer: Thus diminishing marginal utility explains why consumers buy more only at lower prices, giving us the law of demand.

questions.q: What is price elasticity of demand, and what factors determine it?

answer.text: measures how much the quantity demanded of a good responds to a change in its price.

list: Demand is elastic if quantity changes a lot when price changes; inelastic if it changes little
It is calculated as the percentage change in quantity divided by the percentage change in price

answer.text: They decide how sensitive buyers are.

list: Goods with close substitutes have elastic demand; necessities without substitutes have inelastic demand
The share of income spent on the good and the time available to adjust also affect elasticity

questions.q: How does a consumer reach equilibrium according to the utility approach?

answer.text: is in equilibrium when they get the maximum satisfaction (utility) from spending their limited income, and buy no more or less.

list: The consumer buys up to the point where the marginal utility of the good equals its price
Beyond that point, extra units give less satisfaction than they cost
The consumer arranges spending so that the marginal utility per rupee is equal across all goods
This equi-marginal principle gives the greatest total satisfaction from the given income
